name: create_draft
description:
Create a new email draft in the user's Outlook account. The draft is saved but NOT sent.
The user can review and send it from Outlook.

Use this tool to compose emails on behalf of the user. The draft-first approach ensures
the user can review the email before it is sent.

To create a reply draft in an existing email thread:
1. First use outlook_get_message to read the original message
2. Set reply_to_message_id to the original message's internet_message_id (NOT the message_id)
3. Set conversation_id to the original message's conversation_id
4. The subject should start with 'Re: ' followed by the original subject

The response returns message_id and web_link. Use the message_id to update the draft
(outlook_update_draft), send it (outlook_send_draft), or verify its contents
(outlook_get_message). You can also use outlook_list_drafts to find drafts later.

After creating the draft, tell the user the draft has been saved and they can
find it in their Outlook Drafts folder to review and send.

to.description: List of recipient email addresses (To field)

cc.description: List of CC recipient email addresses (optional)

bcc.description: List of BCC recipient email addresses (optional)

body.description: Plain text body of the email

body_html.description: Optional: HTML body. If provided, email body is set as HTML content type.

reply_to_message_id.description: Optional: RFC Message-ID for threading replies (use internet_message_id from outlook_get_message, NOT the message_id). Sets In-Reply-To header.

conversation_id.description: Optional: conversation ID to associate this draft with (for threading replies)
